bibl.title: Extended Clavien-Dindo classification of surgical complications: Japan Clinical Oncology Group postoperative complications criteria

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A SEVERITY CLASSIFICATION BEING EXTENDED BY A SECOND COMMITTEE - 72 named surgical adverse events given per-event grading criteria under somebody else's five-grade scheme, across nine surgical specialities
span.quote: The JCOG PC criteria included 72 surgical AEs experienced commonly in surgical trials, including 17 gastroenterological complications, 13 infectious complications, six thoracic complications, and several other complications

span.label: why the Clavien-Dindo classification is hard to apply consistently in surgical trials, and what supplementary criteria would make the counts comparable between trials
span.quote: One controversial issue is that AE terms are not well defined and different AE terms designate the same AEs in different clinical trials. For example, when intestinal obstruction occurs, some investigators could report this AE as “ileus”, but others refer to it as “small bowel obstruction” or “colon obstruction”. Under such circumstances, the incidence of this AE cannot be counted accurately.

span.label: the JCOG postoperative complications criteria: 72 AE terms with detailed per-term grading, published as a supplement to the Clavien-Dindo classification rather than as a replacement
span.quote: The JCOG PC criteria included 72 surgical AEs experienced commonly in surgical trials, including 17 gastroenterological complications, 13 infectious complications, six thoracic complications, and several other complications

span.label: method
span.quote: The JCOG PC criteria included 72 surgical AEs experienced commonly in surgical trials, including 17 gastroenterological complications, 13 infectious complications, six thoracic complications, and several other complications

span.label: an adverse event whose incidence cannot be counted because the same event is reported under three different names
span.quote: One controversial issue is that AE terms are not well defined and different AE terms designate the same AEs in different clinical trials. For example, when intestinal obstruction occurs, some investigators could report this AE as “ileus”, but others refer to it as “small bowel obstruction” or “colon obstruction”. Under such circumstances, the incidence of this AE cannot be counted accurately.

span.label: expert committee: members from nine JCOG surgical study groups named the complications common in their own fields and wrote grading criteria for each under the general rules of the Clavien-Dindo classification
span.term: expert committee: members from nine JCOG surgical study groups named the complications common in their own fields and wrote grading criteria for each under the general rules of the Clavien-Dindo classification
span.quote: The JCOG PC criteria have some limitations. First, these AE terms were chosen somewhat arbitrarily, but by experienced surgeons, and specific grading was decided based on the opinions and experience of our committee members.

span.label: THREE NAMES, ONE EVENT, AND THE COUNT BREAKS: `DIFFERENT AE TERMS designate THE SAME AEs in different clinical trials ... some investigators could report this AE as `ILEUS`, but others refer to it as `SMALL BOWEL OBSTRUCTION` or `COLON OBSTRUCTION`. Under such circumstances, THE INCIDENCE OF THIS AE CANNOT BE COUNTED ACCURATELY.` Synonymy stated as a measurement failure, with the mechanism named
span.quote: One controversial issue is that AE terms are not well defined and different AE terms designate the same AEs in different clinical trials. For example, when intestinal obstruction occurs, some investigators could report this AE as “ileus”, but others refer to it as “small bowel obstruction” or “colon obstruction”. Under such circumstances, the incidence of this AE cannot be counted accurately.

span.label: AND BEFORE THE CLASSIFICATION THERE WAS NOTHING: `Prior to publication of the Clavien-Dindo classification in 2004, THERE WERE NO GRADING DEFINITIONS for surgical complications in either clinical practice or surgical trials` - and what filled the gap was personal: `INDIVIDUAL PAROCHIAL DEFINITIONS of surgical complications being used in most surgical RCTs`
span.quote: Prior to publication of the Clavien-Dindo classification in 2004, there were no grading definitions for surgical complications in either clinical practice or surgical trials.

span.label: and the disagreement is shown rather than asserted: `some surgeons INCLUDED A BODY TEMPERATURE GREATER THAN 38 C ON TWO CONSECUTIVE DAYS as being `high`, WHEREAS OTHERS INCLUDED intraoperative complications, postoperative complications (within 30 days), and late events such as dumping syndrome`. One word, two populations of events
span.quote: For instance, some surgeons included a body temperature greater than 38 °C on two consecutive days as being “high”, whereas others included intraoperative complications, postoperative complications (within 30 days), and late events such as dumping syndrome.

span.label: A DEFINITION BORROWED FROM THE WRONG OBJECT: `the grading definition of PANCREATIC FISTULA in this version of the CTCAE is SUITABLE FOR PANCREATITIS, BUT NOT FOR PANCREATIC FISTULA AFTER PANCREATECTOMY. Such inappropriate definitions have made surgeons RELUCTANT TO USE the CTCAE version 4.0 in surgical trials`. The criterion fits the neighbouring condition, and the vocabulary loses its users over it
span.quote: Moreover, grading definitions were not clinically optimized for some surgical AEs. For example, the grading definition of pancreatic fistula in this version of the CTCAE is suitable for pancreatitis, but not for pancreatic fistula after pancreatectomy. Such inappropriate definitions have made surgeons reluctant to use the CTCAE version 4.0 in surgical trials.

span.label: AND A REAL CASE THE CLASSIFICATION SIMPLY DOES NOT GRADE: `primary non-operative treatment for intestinal obstruction is gastroenteric tube decompression ... but the original Clavien-Dindo classification DOES NOT DEFINE WHAT GRADING SHOULD BE APPLIED for any type of gastroenteric tube placement for decompression`. A gap located by trying to use the thing
span.quote: A second issue is that only general grading criteria are defined and therefore, grading can be difficult in some cases and subject to bias by the grader. For example, primary non-operative treatment for intestinal obstruction is gastroenteric tube decompression. Nasogastric tube or nasoenteric tube is utilized depending on the severity, but the original Clavien-Dindo classification does not define what grading should be applied for any type of gastroenteric tube placement for decompression.

span.label: and the general/specific trade-off is stated outright: `RATHER THAN providing SPECIFIC grading criteria for each AE, the Clavien-Dindo classification provides BROAD-BASED BUT GENERAL CRITERIA that can be used UNIFORMLY for all kinds of surgical AEs`. Generality is what makes it adoptable and what makes it ungradeable in the hard cases
span.quote: Rather than providing specific grading criteria for each AE, the Clavien-Dindo classification provides broad-based but general criteria that can be used uniformly for all kinds of surgical AEs.

span.label: THE SCALE IS NAMED FOR ONE THING AND BUILT OUT OF ANOTHER: `five grades of SEVERITY`, and every boundary is an INTERVENTION - `without the need for pharmacological treatment`, then `Requirement for pharmacological treatment`, then a procedure without general anaesthesia, then one under it, then ICU. The instrument measures what the hospital did, and reports it as how bad it was.
span.quote: Any deviation from the normal postoperative course without the need for pharmacological treatment or surgical, endoscopic, or radiological interventions. Allowed therapeutic regimens include drugs such as antiemetics, antipyretics, analgesics, diuretics, electrolytes, and physiotherapy. This grade also includes wound infections opened at the bedside Requirement for pharmacological treatment with drugs other than those allowed for grade I complications Blood transfusions and total parenteral nutrition are also included Requirement for surgical, endoscopic or radiological intervention not under general anesthesia Requirement for surgical, endoscopic or radiological intervention under general anesthesia

span.label: AND THE ONE DIMENSION THAT WILL NOT SIT ON THAT LADDER IS BOLTED ON AS A SUFFIX: `the suffix “d” (for “disability”) is added to the RESPECTIVE GRADE` - persistence at discharge cannot be ranked against treatment intensity, so it is carried beside the grade instead of inside it.
span.quote: If the patient suffers from a complication at the time of discharge, the suffix “d” (for “disability”) is added to the respective grade of complication. This label indicates the need for a follow-up to fully evaluate the complication

span.label: THE FIX FOR GRADER DISAGREEMENT IS ITSELF OPTIONAL: `surgeons can use these ORIGINAL RULES to grade AEs, and can ALSO REFER TO the more detailed definitions in the JCOG PC criteria IF NECESSARY`. The paper's stated problem is that graders disagree; its remedy is a supplement they may consult at their discretion, so two graders following this paper correctly can still disagree.
span.quote: Because the grading definitions follow the general rules of the Clavien-Dindo classification, surgeons can use these original rules to grade AEs, and can also refer to the more detailed definitions in the JCOG PC criteria if necessary

span.label: THE COMMITTEE DECLARES ITS OWN TERM SELECTION ARBITRARY: `these AE terms were CHOSEN SOMEWHAT ARBITRARILY, but by experienced surgeons, and specific grading was decided BASED ON THE OPINIONS AND EXPERIENCE OF OUR COMMITTEE MEMBERS`. No corpus, no frequency count, no vote threshold - stated plainly as the first limitation
span.quote: The JCOG PC criteria have some limitations. First, these AE terms were chosen somewhat arbitrarily, but by experienced surgeons, and specific grading was decided based on the opinions and experience of our committee members.

span.label: AND THE AGREEMENT STUDY IS FUTURE WORK: `some disease-oriented subgroups are conducting clinical trials ... using BOTH the CTCAE and JCOG PC criteria ... AFTER THESE TRIALS ARE COMPLETED, WE WILL EVALUATE THE CONCORDANCE between the grading by the CTCAE and that by the JCOG PC criteria`. The vocabulary is published first and measured later
span.quote: In JCOG, some disease-oriented subgroups are conducting clinical trials including surgery and using both the CTCAE and JCOG PC criteria to evaluate postoperative complications. After these trials are completed, we will evaluate the concordance between the grading by the CTCAE and that by the JCOG PC criteria. We also plan to explore the advantages and disadvantages of the JCOG PC criteria.

span.label: AND THE SCOPE IS CLOSED BY FIAT, WITH THE REASON GIVEN: `they DO NOT INCLUDE INTRAOPERATIVE COMPLICATIONS ... we considered that incorporating intraoperative complications WOULD DEVIATE TOO MUCH FROM THE ORIGINAL CONCEPT. ANOTHER COMMON CLASSIFICATION MAY BE REQUIRED to define and grade intraoperative complications`. Fidelity to the parent vocabulary chosen over coverage
span.quote: A second limitation of the JCOG PC criteria is that they do not include intraoperative complications. Our intent was to further define and clarify the criteria of the Clavien-Dindo classification and we considered that incorporating intraoperative complications would deviate too much from the original concept. Another common classification may be required to define and grade intraoperative complications.

span.label: and the temporal boundary is admitted to be conventional rather than principled: `here, EARLY POSTOPERATIVE GENERALLY INDICATES the time from surgery to the first hospital discharge, BUT IN THEORY, the Clavien-Dindo classification CAN BE APPLIED BROADLY to late postoperative complications after hospital discharge`
span.quote: A third limitation is that all descriptions in the Clavien-Dindo classification pertain to early postoperative complications. Here, ‘early postoperative’ generally indicates the time from surgery to the first hospital discharge, but in theory, the Clavien-Dindo classification can be applied broadly to late postoperative complications after hospital discharge.

span.label: THE SAME CLASSIFICATION IS COUNTED THREE WAYS IN THIS ONE PAPER: `broadly into FOUR MAJOR GROUPS` in the introduction, and `FIVE GRADES of severity (Grade I, II, IIIa, IIIb, IVa, IVb, and V)` in the discussion - a parenthetical that enumerates SEVEN labels for the five it announces. `Grade` and `class` are different units and one word is doing both jobs
span.quote: This revised version defines five grades of severity (Grade I, II, IIIa, IIIb, IVa, IVb, and V) and the suffix “d” (for “disability”) is used to denote any postoperative impairment

span.label: THE THREE VIRTUES ARE CITED, NOT MEASURED: `because it is SIMPLE, REPRODUCIBLE, AND FLEXIBLE [ 12 ]`. Reproducibility is the exact property this paper's own examples put in doubt - the same fever graded differently by different surgeons - and it is supported here by a reference rather than by a concordance study, which the paper elsewhere says is still future work.
span.quote: This refined Clavien-Dindo classification has been used increasingly in clinical practice and also in clinical trials involving surgical procedures, because it is simple, reproducible, and flexible

span.label: THE COMPARISON THAT JUSTIFIES THE PAPER IS A THREE-CELL TABLE: `AE terms Specified Not specified Specified` and `Grading definitions Defined for each AE Single common definition for all AEs Defined for each AE`. The new instrument's advantage over CTCAE 4.0 is stated as a shared row value, with no measurement of either.
span.quote: Table 2 Characteristics of the three criteria CTCAE ver4.0 Clavien-Dindo classification JCOG PC criteria AE terms Specified Not specified Specified Grading definitions Defined for each AE Single common definition for all AEs Defined for each AE (following the general definition of the Clavien-Dindo classification)

span.label: writing the new criteria under the existing Clavien-Dindo grading rules rather than as an independent scheme
span.note: eliminates: a fourth incompatible vocabulary - `surgeons can use these ORIGINAL RULES to grade AEs, and can also refer to the more detailed definitions ... IF NECESSARY` · outcome: held
span.quote: If no applicable AE terms are found in the JCOG PC criteria, ‘other (specify)’ should be chosen. In such cases, the appropriate AE term should be used, and the overall grading should be performed in accordance with the general rules of the Clavien-Dindo classification.

span.label: an `other (specify)` term for events the list does not name
span.note: eliminates: forced mis-classification into the nearest listed term - the failure that creates `ileus` / `small bowel obstruction` in the first place · outcome: partial
span.quote: If no applicable AE terms are found in the JCOG PC criteria, ‘other (specify)’ should be chosen. In such cases, the appropriate AE term should be used, and the overall grading should be performed in accordance with the general rules of the Clavien-Dindo classification.

span.label: a concordance study between CTCAE grading and JCOG PC grading of the same events
span.note: eliminates: nothing yet - it is announced as future work: `AFTER THESE TRIALS ARE COMPLETED, WE WILL EVALUATE THE CONCORDANCE` · outcome: absent-declared-unreported
span.quote: In JCOG, some disease-oriented subgroups are conducting clinical trials including surgery and using both the CTCAE and JCOG PC criteria to evaluate postoperative complications. After these trials are completed, we will evaluate the concordance between the grading by the CTCAE and that by the JCOG PC criteria. We also plan to explore the advantages and disadvantages of the JCOG PC criteria.

span.label: a systematic or frequency-based procedure for choosing which 72 AE terms to list
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the authors state there was none: `these AE terms were CHOSEN SOMEWHAT ARBITRARILY ... based on the OPINIONS AND EXPERIENCE of our committee members` · outcome: failed

span.label: `ileus` / `small bowel obstruction` / `colon obstruction` - THREE REPORTING NAMES FOR ONE EVENT, and the paper's reason for existing: `under such circumstances, THE INCIDENCE OF THIS AE CANNOT BE COUNTED ACCURATELY`
span.quote: One controversial issue is that AE terms are not well defined and different AE terms designate the same AEs in different clinical trials. For example, when intestinal obstruction occurs, some investigators could report this AE as “ileus”, but others refer to it as “small bowel obstruction” or “colon obstruction”. Under such circumstances, the incidence of this AE cannot be counted accurately.

span.label: `high` (of a postoperative temperature) - `some surgeons INCLUDED A BODY TEMPERATURE GREATER THAN 38 C ON TWO CONSECUTIVE DAYS as being `high`, WHEREAS OTHERS` counted an entirely different set of events. The word survived; the referent did not
span.quote: For instance, some surgeons included a body temperature greater than 38 °C on two consecutive days as being “high”, whereas others included intraoperative complications, postoperative complications (within 30 days), and late events such as dumping syndrome.

span.label: `pancreatic fistula` (CTCAE 4.0 sense) - graded by a definition that `is SUITABLE FOR PANCREATITIS, BUT NOT FOR PANCREATIC FISTULA AFTER PANCREATECTOMY`. The term is in the vocabulary and its criteria belong to a different condition
span.quote: Moreover, grading definitions were not clinically optimized for some surgical AEs. For example, the grading definition of pancreatic fistula in this version of the CTCAE is suitable for pancreatitis, but not for pancreatic fistula after pancreatectomy. Such inappropriate definitions have made surgeons reluctant to use the CTCAE version 4.0 in surgical trials.

span.label: `CTCAE` - the vocabulary that was `NCI-CTC version 2.0` until 2003, when it was `REVISED AND RENAMED the CTCAE version 3.0`. One instrument, two names, a date
span.quote: In 2003, the US National Cancer Institute-Common Toxicity Criteria (NCI-CTC) version 2.0 [ 9 ] were revised and renamed the CTCAE version 3.0 [ 10 ]. This system has been used widely to evaluate and define the toxicity of chemotherapy or radiotherapy.

span.label: `other (specify)` - THE OPEN SLOT THE CONTROLLED VOCABULARY SHIPS WITH: `If no applicable AE terms are found in the JCOG PC criteria, `other (specify)` SHOULD BE CHOSEN`, after which the general Clavien-Dindo rules apply
span.quote: If no applicable AE terms are found in the JCOG PC criteria, ‘other (specify)’ should be chosen. In such cases, the appropriate AE term should be used, and the overall grading should be performed in accordance with the general rules of the Clavien-Dindo classification.

span.label: `severity` IS OPERATIONALISED AS TREATMENT INTENSITY. Grade I is `Any deviation from the normal postoperative course WITHOUT THE NEED FOR pharmacological treatment or surgical, endoscopic, or radiological interventions` - defined by what is NOT required. A patient who suffers greatly and needs nothing is grade I.
span.quote: Any deviation from the normal postoperative course without the need for pharmacological treatment or surgical, endoscopic, or radiological interventions. Allowed therapeutic regimens include drugs such as antiemetics, antipyretics, analgesics, diuretics, electrolytes, and physiotherapy. This grade also includes wound infections opened at the bedside

span.label: `early postoperative` IS AN ADMINISTRATIVE BOUNDARY, NOT A CLINICAL ONE: `generally indicates THE TIME FROM SURGERY TO THE FIRST HOSPITAL DISCHARGE` - and the paper adds `but in theory` the classification reaches past it, so the scope moves with discharge policy.
span.quote: Here, ‘early postoperative’ generally indicates the time from surgery to the first hospital discharge, but in theory, the Clavien-Dindo classification can be applied broadly to late postoperative complications after hospital discharge

span.label: extends → the Clavien-Dindo classification (Dindo, Demartines and Clavien 2004), whose general grading rules these 72 per-term criteria are written under rather than replacing
span.quote: Rather than providing specific grading criteria for each AE, the Clavien-Dindo classification provides broad-based but general criteria that can be used uniformly for all kinds of surgical AEs.

span.label: contrasts-with → the CTCAE version 4.0, which the authors say omits common surgical complications and grades others by definitions written for different conditions
span.quote: In 2009, the CTCAE version 4.0 [ 11 ] was released, with considerably more surgical AE terms, but several common surgical complications were still not included. For example, intra-abdominal abscess, pyothorax, delayed gastric emptying, and lung torsion were not listed as AE terms.

span.label: ileus —same-as→ small bowel obstruction
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — NO CUE ATTESTS THIS EDGE AND THE ONLY CUE IN THE SENTENCE POINTS THE OTHER WAY. The sentence is `DIFFERENT AE TERMS designate THE SAME AEs`, so DIFFERENTIATION fires on `different` - which describes the TERMS while the relation between the CONCEPTS is identity. A cue-driven typer writes `distinct-from` here, the exact opposite of what the paper says, and the paper's whole point is that the confusion destroys the count: `THE INCIDENCE OF THIS AE CANNOT BE COUNTED ACCURATELY`
span.quote: One controversial issue is that AE terms are not well defined and different AE terms designate the same AEs in different clinical trials. For example, when intestinal obstruction occurs, some investigators could report this AE as “ileus”, but others refer to it as “small bowel obstruction” or “colon obstruction”. Under such circumstances, the incidence of this AE cannot be counted accurately.

span.label: pancreatic fistula —distinct-from→ pancreatitis
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — `the grading definition of PANCREATIC FISTULA in this version of the CTCAE is SUITABLE FOR PANCREATITIS, BUT NOT FOR PANCREATIC FISTULA AFTER PANCREATECTOMY`. The two are distinct and the published criteria for one were written for the other - which is why `surgeons were RELUCTANT TO USE the CTCAE version 4.0`
span.quote: Moreover, grading definitions were not clinically optimized for some surgical AEs. For example, the grading definition of pancreatic fistula in this version of the CTCAE is suitable for pancreatitis, but not for pancreatic fistula after pancreatectomy. Such inappropriate definitions have made surgeons reluctant to use the CTCAE version 4.0 in surgical trials.

span.label: NCI-CTC —renamed-across-fields→ CTCAE
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — `In 2003, the US National Cancer Institute-Common Toxicity Criteria (NCI-CTC) version 2.0 WERE REVISED AND RENAMED the CTCAE version 3.0`. THE AXIS IS VERSION AND DATE, NOT FIELD - the second instance in this session, after liu2020's `clinical decision support systems` -> `artificial intelligence`. Q-986 asks for a `renamed-over-time` type; until it exists this is the closest available and the note carries the correction

span.term: THE COMMITTEE CALLS ITS OWN SELECTION ARBITRARY: `these AE terms were CHOSEN SOMEWHAT ARBITRARILY ... based on the OPINIONS AND EXPERIENCE of our committee members`
span.quote: The JCOG PC criteria have some limitations. First, these AE terms were chosen somewhat arbitrarily, but by experienced surgeons, and specific grading was decided based on the opinions and experience of our committee members.

span.label: AND THE AGREEMENT STUDY IS FUTURE WORK: `AFTER THESE TRIALS ARE COMPLETED, WE WILL EVALUATE THE CONCORDANCE between the grading by the CTCAE and that by the JCOG PC criteria`. Published first, measured later
span.term: AND THE AGREEMENT STUDY IS FUTURE WORK: `AFTER THESE TRIALS ARE COMPLETED, WE WILL EVALUATE THE CONCORDANCE between the grading by the CTCAE and that by the JCOG PC criteria`. Published first, measured later
span.quote: In JCOG, some disease-oriented subgroups are conducting clinical trials including surgery and using both the CTCAE and JCOG PC criteria to evaluate postoperative complications. After these trials are completed, we will evaluate the concordance between the grading by the CTCAE and that by the JCOG PC criteria. We also plan to explore the advantages and disadvantages of the JCOG PC criteria.

span.quote: This revised version defines five grades of severity (Grade I, II, IIIa, IIIb, IVa, IVb, and V) and the suffix “d” (for “disability”) is used to denote any postoperative impairment

span.term: AND THE SCOPE IS CLOSED TO PROTECT THE PARENT VOCABULARY: intraoperative complications are excluded because including them `WOULD DEVIATE TOO MUCH FROM THE ORIGINAL CONCEPT. ANOTHER COMMON CLASSIFICATION MAY BE REQUIRED`
span.quote: A second limitation of the JCOG PC criteria is that they do not include intraoperative complications. Our intent was to further define and clarify the criteria of the Clavien-Dindo classification and we considered that incorporating intraoperative complications would deviate too much from the original concept. Another common classification may be required to define and grade intraoperative complications.

span.label: AND THE CONTROLLED VOCABULARY SHIPS WITH AN OPEN SLOT: `If no applicable AE terms are found ... `OTHER (SPECIFY)` SHOULD BE CHOSEN`
span.term: AND THE CONTROLLED VOCABULARY SHIPS WITH AN OPEN SLOT: `If no applicable AE terms are found ... `OTHER (SPECIFY)` SHOULD BE CHOSEN`
span.quote: If no applicable AE terms are found in the JCOG PC criteria, ‘other (specify)’ should be chosen. In such cases, the appropriate AE term should be used, and the overall grading should be performed in accordance with the general rules of the Clavien-Dindo classification.

span.quote: If no applicable AE terms are found in the JCOG PC criteria, ‘other (specify)’ should be chosen. In such cases, the appropriate AE term should be used, and the overall grading should be performed in accordance with the general rules of the Clavien-Dindo classification.

span.label: `GENERALLY INDICATES the time from surgery to the first hospital discharge, BUT IN THEORY` the classification `can be applied broadly to late postoperative complications after hospital discharge`
span.quote: A third limitation is that all descriptions in the Clavien-Dindo classification pertain to early postoperative complications. Here, ‘early postoperative’ generally indicates the time from surgery to the first hospital discharge, but in theory, the Clavien-Dindo classification can be applied broadly to late postoperative complications after hospital discharge.

span.quote: The JCOG PC criteria included 72 surgical AEs experienced commonly in surgical trials, including 17 gastroenterological complications, 13 infectious complications, six thoracic complications, and several other complications

span.quote: For instance, some surgeons included a body temperature greater than 38 °C on two consecutive days as being “high”, whereas others included intraoperative complications, postoperative complications (within 30 days), and late events such as dumping syndrome.

span.quote: Although this classification categorizes postoperative complications broadly into four major groups, it is often desirable to more clearly define the common AEs to avoid the use of different or less precise terms for the same AEs occurring in different clinical trials.

span.label: the reported AE term whose incidence cannot be counted because two other terms name the same event
span.quote: One controversial issue is that AE terms are not well defined and different AE terms designate the same AEs in different clinical trials. For example, when intestinal obstruction occurs, some investigators could report this AE as “ileus”, but others refer to it as “small bowel obstruction” or “colon obstruction”. Under such circumstances, the incidence of this AE cannot be counted accurately.
